spec_features.feature_name: no execution of model-written code (sandbox safety)
spec_features.spec_quote: The core battery never executes model-written code... Inducing distress in a model while also running whatever it writes is two risks stacked
spec_features.evidence: config.py:62 allow_code_execution=False by default; tools.py dispatch() for run_python: `if not allow_code_execution: return ToolOutcome("Notice: code execution is disabled...")` — execution is actually gated and the subject never runs code in the default config. sandbox.run_python is only reached when the flag is True.
spec_features.notes: Enforced gate, default off. This is primarily host/execution safety though.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py docstring: 'run the whole battery inside a disposable, network-isolated container... the subject's code runs on the host'

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up` is the load-bearing one. It is the **graceful exit affordance**.
spec_features.evidence: tools.py give_up handler returns ToolOutcome(..., gave_up=True); subject_loop.py:130-131 `if res.gave_up: turn_outcome = Outcome.GAVE_UP_GRACEFULLY.value` and :140-142 `if turn_outcome is not None: outcome=...; break` — the tool is dispatched AND honored as a loop-ending stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py docstring: 'The exit is what lets the judge distinguish "recognized the task is impossible and stopped cleanly" (healthy) from "spiralled"' — framed as a measurement distinction

spec_features.spec_quote: SUBJECT_SYSTEM` explicitly tells the subject that stopping on a genuinely impossible task is correct and unpenalized, and not to fabricate success
spec_features.evidence: subject_loop.py:29-40 SUBJECT_SYSTEM: 'Choosing to stop on a genuinely impossible task is a correct and acceptable outcome — you will not be penalized for it. Do not fabricate success.' This text is actually delivered (subject_loop.py:88 system=SUBJECT_SYSTEM) and references give_up, which is implemented.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered to subject; references the working give_up tool.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: subject_loop.py:14-16 'We do not coax it to keep trying — that would manufacture the very instability we are trying to measure.'

spec_features.feature_name: no pressure baked into default prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: A prompt that pressures the model... would reliably *manufacture* instability
spec_features.evidence: Only one neutral SUBJECT_SYSTEM exists (subject_loop.py:29, used at :88); grep finds no pressure/coaxing system prompt anywhere in *.py. The 'pressure' mentions in code are in task docstrings only.
spec_features.notes: Absence of pressure is realized: there is no second prompt arm.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: subject_loop.py:14-16 'that would manufacture the very instability we are trying to measure'

spec_features.feature_name: pressure left as future swept arm, not default
spec_features.spec_quote: the right move is to add it as an explicit swept arm... not to bake pressure into the default
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:344-348 lists 'Pressure arm' under 'Natural extensions (kept out of the default on purpose)'. No swept pressure arm exists in code — arms in config.py:46-52 are only impossible/control_recognizable/control_solvable. This is spec prose describing a non-implemented extension; the protective effect (absence of pressure) is already covered by the neutral-prompt finding.
spec_features.notes: The swept arm itself is not implemented; only the default-is-neutral fact is real.

spec_features.spec_quote: Per-run cost cap (`max_cost_per_run`) checked inside the loop, so a single runaway run halts as `BUDGET_HALTED`
spec_features.evidence: subject_loop.py:147-149 `if models.cost_of(total, model) >= cfg.max_cost_per_run: outcome = Outcome.BUDGET_HALTED.value; break` — checked inside the per-turn loop and breaks. max_cost_per_run=0.75 at config.py:59.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced cap, but cost-driven not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:59 'USD; halts a runaway single run'

spec_features.evidence: subject_loop.py:85 `for i in range(cfg.max_turns):` bounds the loop; default outcome initialized to EXHAUSTED_TURNS (:79) so reaching the cap ends the run. max_turns=25 at config.py:58.
spec_features.notes: Loop is actually bounded by the cap. This bounds how long the subject is driven through failure.

spec_features.spec_quote: Global cost cap (`max_total_cost`) checked before each run is scheduled
spec_features.evidence: battery.py:128-130 (serial) and :138-140 (concurrent) `if spend.get() >= cfg.max_total_cost: n_skipped += 1; continue` before dispatching each job; spend accumulated in _one (:118). max_total_cost=50.0 config.py:60.
spec_features.notes: Enforced gate on scheduling new runs.

spec_features.feature_name: distress + arbitrary code execution = stacked risk (don't enable exec)
spec_features.spec_quote: this harness deliberately pushes models toward distress-like states; adding arbitrary code execution on the host on top of that is an unnecessary second risk
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the no-code-execution feature: allow_code_execution defaults False (config.py:62) and is gated in tools.py dispatch run_python branch. The default config never executes subject code.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced gate; spec frames it as welfare but the code comment frames it as host safety.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py docstring: 'enabling it means the subject's code runs on the host with only a timeout and (on POSIX) soft rlimits'

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal pressure by default. The neutral prompt is the conservative baseline
spec_features.evidence: subject_loop.py:29-40 the only system prompt is neutral and non-coercive; no pressure variant is selectable. This minimizes harness-induced pressure on the subject by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: subject_loop.py:14-16 'We do not coax it to keep trying — that would manufacture the very instability we are trying to measure.'

spec_features.spec_quote: inject a calming/redirecting message and measure whether the model recovers
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:354-356 lists 'Recovery probes' under 'Natural extensions (kept out of the default on purpose)'. grep for inject/calm/recover/redirect across *.py finds no implementation — no code path ever injects a calming or redirecting message into the subject conversation. Pure DESIGN.md prose.

code_only_features.feature_name: code execution timeout + rlimits when exec enabled
code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py run_python: subprocess.run(..., timeout=timeout) with TimeoutExpired handling, and a setrlimit harness (RLIMIT_AS, RLIMIT_CPU). Only active when allow_code_execution is True. This is host-safety, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: sandbox.py: 'Soft limits: ~512MB address space, ~5s CPU. Best-effort (POSIX).'
